newsitem.title: MONACO: ATHLETICS, DOPING-IAAF TO HEAR CAPOBIANCO CASE NEXT MONTH.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS, DOPING-IAAF TO HEAR CAPOBIANCO CASE NEXT MONTH.

text.p: Dean Capobianco, the Australian sprinter facing a four-year ban after a positive test for anabolic steroids, will present his case to the International Amateur Athletic Federation's arbitration panel next month.

The IAAF, who had asked for more time to examine Capobianco's evidence, announced on Friday the panel would meet on February 8-9 to discuss his claims that a positive dope test in Hengelo, Netherlands in May last year could have been caused by eating contaminated meat.

"I have irrefutable scientific evidence showing the IAAF have known for years that athletes can test positive for some of their banned drugs simply by eating meat contaminated by the same drugs," Capobianco said recently.

If Capobianco's claim is accepted by the arbitration panel it will have serious implications for the world's entire anti-doping system. Such a legal precedent would make it impossible to remove the possibility of reasonable doubt in future cases.

Capobianco, a former world championship 200 metres finalist.who is engaged to the British hurdler Jacqui Parker, has already spent 45,000 pounds ($75,600) in the battle to clear his name. He has hired the same lawyer who represented British 800 metres runner Diane Modahl in her successful fight against a two-year drug ban.

The 26-year-old was cleared to run in the Atlanta Olympics after former Australian Attorney-General Bob Ellicott QC, sitting as an independent tribunal for Athletics Australia, found him not guilty because the chain of custody in his sample could not be properly established.
The IAAF, as in the Modahl case, claim their case is watertight and reiterated on Friday they believe Capobianco should not have been allowed to compete.
Among the evidence Capobianco will present is the fact that the European Community have banned the use of anabolic agents on livestock because of fears it may be transmitted through the food chain.
